title: Water and Changes of State
seo_title: Primary 5 Science: Water and Changes of State Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 5: Cycles in matter and water (Water: changes of state)
standard_text: Recognise that water can exist in three states and that it changes from one state to another when it gains or loses heat: melting, freezing, boiling, evaporation and condensation. Investigate the factors that affect the rate of evaporation: temperature, wind, exposed surface area and humidity (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on water and changes of state: melting, freezing, boiling, evaporation, condensation and factors affecting evaporation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Water changes state when it gains or loses heat.
body_html:
How to think about it

Water can change from one state to another when it gains or loses heat.

  • Heat gain: melting (ice → water, at 0 °C), boiling (water → water vapour, at 100 °C), evaporation (water → water vapour, at any temperature).
  • Heat loss: freezing (water → ice, at 0 °C), condensation (water vapour → water, on cold surfaces).
  • Evaporation is faster when it is hotter, windier, drier and when more surface is exposed.
Example

Droplets form on a cold can. Where did the water come from?

Water vapour in the air touches the cold can

It loses heat and condenses

Answer: From the air.

Example

Wet clothes dry faster on a windy day. Why?

Wind carries water vapour away

More water can evaporate

Answer: Wind speeds up evaporation.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the water on a cold can leaked through it. It condensed from the air.
  • Thinking evaporation needs 100 °C. It happens at any temperature.
  • Calling the white mist above a kettle 'water vapour'. Water vapour is invisible; the mist is tiny droplets.
  • Mixing up boiling and evaporation. Boiling happens throughout the liquid at 100 °C; evaporation is only at the surface.

faq.q: What is the difference between evaporation and boiling?
faq.a: Evaporation happens at any temperature, only at the surface of the water. Boiling happens at 100 °C throughout the water, with bubbles.

faq.q: Why do water droplets form on a cold glass?
faq.a: Water vapour in the air loses heat to the cold glass and condenses into water droplets.
A higher temperature, more wind, a larger exposed surface area and drier air (lower humidity).

items.q: During condensation, does water gain heat or lose heat?
c: It gains heat and loses heat equally.
items.e: Condensation: gas → liquid.

items.q: What is water vapour?
c: water in the gas state, which is invisible
items.e: We cannot see water vapour.

items.q: Which word describes a liquid changing into a gas?
items.e: Melting, freezing, evaporating (and boiling), condensing.

items.q: Which word describes a liquid changing into a solid?
items.e: Melting, freezing, evaporating (and boiling), condensing.

items.q: At what temperature does pure water boil?
items.e: At boiling point, water changes into water vapour quickly.

items.q: What is the temperature at which pure water freezes?
items.e: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius (°C).

from a solid to a gas
from a liquid to a gas
from a gas to a liquid
items.e: Evaporation changes water from a liquid to a gas.

items.q: What happens to the temperature of ice while it is melting?
c: It stays at 0 °C until all the ice has melted.
items.e: The heat gained is used to change the state.

items.q: What is boiling?

a liquid changing into a gas when it is heated quickly
a liquid changing into a solid when it is cooled
a solid changing into a liquid when it is heated
items.e: Changes of state happen when materials are heated or cooled.

items.q: Why do clothes dry faster when they are spread out than when folded?

items.e: Exposed surface area affects the rate of evaporation.

items.q: During evaporation, does water gain heat or lose heat?

items.e: Evaporation: liquid → gas.

items.q: Which processes involve heat loss?
items.e: Heat is lost when a gas becomes a liquid or a liquid becomes a solid.

items.q: Why do we feel cool after swimming on a windy day?
c: Water on our skin evaporates and takes heat from our body.
items.e: Evaporation causes cooling.

items.q: Which processes involve heat gain?
items.e: Heat is needed to change a solid to a liquid or a liquid to a gas.

items.q: The bathroom mirror becomes misty after a hot shower. Which process is this?

items.q: Which shows the correct order when ice is heated until it boils?
items.e: Melting first, then boiling.

items.q: What is the white 'steam' we see above a boiling kettle?
c: tiny water droplets formed when water vapour cools
items.e: Water vapour is invisible; the white mist is condensed droplets.

items.q: Which happens only at 100 °C for pure water?
items.e: Evaporation can happen at any temperature.

items.q: Which can happen at room temperature?
items.e: Puddles dry without boiling.

items.q: Water is left in an open dish in a classroom at 30 °C. Will it evaporate?
c: Yes, slowly, even though it is below 100 °C.
items.e: Evaporation happens at any temperature.

items.q: Spectacles mist up when you walk out of an air-conditioned room. Which process is this?
items.e: Condensation: gas → liquid (heat loss).

items.q: Why do wet clothes dry slowly on a rainy day?
c: There is no sunlight at all.
The air already has a lot of water vapour.
items.e: Humid air slows down evaporation.

items.q: Which happens only at the surface of the water?
items.e: Boiling happens throughout the water, with bubbles.

items.q: Why does a bathroom mirror mist up after a hot shower?
c: Warm water vapour condenses on the cooler mirror.
items.e: The mirror is cooler than the water vapour.

items.q: Water droplets appear on the inside of a lunch box lid. What happened?
c: Water vapour from the warm food condensed on the cooler lid.
items.e: Water vapour loses heat to the lid.

items.q: Water droplets form on the outside of a glass of iced water. Where did the water come from?
c: the ice melting through the glass
water vapour in the air that condensed on the cold glass
items.e: Water vapour loses heat to the cold glass and condenses.

items.q: Why does a glass of iced water become wet on the outside on a humid day in Singapore?
c: The glass leaks more on humid days.
The ice evaporates out of the glass.
There is a lot of water vapour in the air to condense on the cold glass.
items.e: Singapore's air is often humid.

items.q: Why is food in a covered pot slow to dry out?
c: The lid makes the food colder.
Water vapour condenses on the lid and drips back.
items.e: The water vapour cannot escape.

items.q: Why do spectacles mist up when you walk from an air-conditioned room into the hot air outside?
c: Water vapour in the warm air condenses on the cold lenses.
items.e: The lenses are colder than the outside air.

items.q: Which happens throughout the liquid, with bubbles forming inside?
items.e: Evaporation is only at the surface.

items.q: A wet floor dries after it is mopped. Which process is this?
items.e: Evaporation: liquid → gas (heat gain).

items.q: Puddles on a school field disappear after the rain stops. Which process is this?
items.e: Evaporation: liquid → gas (heat gain).

items.q: Sweat on your skin dries on a breezy day. Which process is this?
items.e: Evaporation: liquid → gas (heat gain).

items.q: Which needs a large amount of heat quickly from a heat source such as a stove?
items.e: Evaporation is slow and can use heat from the surroundings.

items.q: An ice kachang melts in the hot sun. Which process is this?
items.e: Melting: solid → liquid (heat gain).
